title: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints 16-01, 18-01, and 19-01 were judicially out of order; the other consolidated complaints were in order. The challenge to Presbytery’s delay in granting West End’s valid dissolution request was sustained, while the challenge to Presbytery’s three-month salary gift was not sustained. The judgment did not separately resolve every remaining complaint by number.
first_summary: Ruling elders challenged James River Presbytery’s delay in honoring West End’s congregational vote to dissolve its pastoral relationship and its three-month salary gift to the pastor. The SJC held that Presbytery lacked a constitutional basis to delay a valid dissolution request but could use its own civil funds for benevolent giving. Several complaints were judicially out of order; the others were in order.
summary: Ruling elders challenged James River Presbytery’s delay in honoring West End’s valid congregational vote to dissolve its pastoral relationship and a three-month salary gift to the pastor. The SJC held that Presbytery lacked a constitutional basis to delay the dissolution, but rejected the challenge to its benevolent use of its own civil funds. Complaints 16-01, 18-01, and 19-01 were judicially out of order; the others were in order. No remand or repayment was ordered. A concurrence cautioned that prompt dissolution is not automatic when objective, justifiable findings support refusal.

sources.supports: Issues, judgment, procedural rulings, dissolution reasoning, and salary-gift ruling.
Adoption by the full SJC and the separate concurrence’s qualification.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The consolidated caption identifies Case 2002-03 and the parties (lines 13–25); the full SJC approved the decision October 22, 2004 (lines 645–655).
evidence_notes.dispute: The stated issues concern delayed dissolution and Presbytery’s salary gift (lines 292–299, printed p. 84).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The judgment identifies out-of-order and in-order complaints, finds no constitutional basis for delay, and upholds the gift (lines 300–324); reasons appear at lines 328–641.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The separate concurrence says dissolution need not be automatic if objective, justifiable findings support refusal (lines 659–671, printed p. 98).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The majority invoked Cases 91-2 and 92-2 for the principle that BCO 23-1 discretion cannot prevent implementation of a valid congregational decision (lines 494–570, printed pp. 91–94).

source_limits: The opinion consolidates three cases and seventeen complaints; its formal judgment addresses grouped issues rather than giving a separate merits disposition for every in-order complaint.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the delayed dissolution and salary gift.
score_reasons.decision: States the successful, unsuccessful, and out-of-order results.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains both the valid congregational request and Presbytery’s control of its civil funds.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the concurrence’s limitation on automatic dissolution.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the majority judgment from the concurrence and avoids assigning unstated issue-level results.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the dispute and outcome.

verification_notes: Rechecked the formal judgment and corrected the synopsis to identify only the three Case 2002-03 complaints expressly ruled judicially out of order, to distinguish the salary-gift ruling from the dissolution ruling, and to label the nonautomatic-dissolution qualification as a separate concurrence. Confirmed that no remand or repayment was ordered.
